Bubble letters, from the oldest block on the site

Enclosed Alphanumerics is an old block, added well before the mathematical alphabets, and its age shows up as good font coverage: capitals from U+24B6, lowercase from U+24D0. The digits have a stranger history. Zero is a lone character of its own, ⓪ at U+24EA, while one through nine come from an earlier range of circled digits, so the ring around a zero is sometimes drawn a little differently from the ring around a nine.

They make usable bullets and step markers in a field with no list formatting, and they are the standard answer when somebody asks for bubble letters for a party invitation or a playful display name. The known gap is Android: some system fonts ship the capitals but not the lowercase set, and a missing character comes out as an empty rectangle. If you cannot predict your readers' devices, capitals are the safer half.

Where Circled text works, and where it does not

WorksVery widely supported — these are long-standing characters and most fonts on most devices have them. Watch outSome Android system fonts miss the lowercase enclosed letters and draw an empty box instead.

Circled questions

Why does the zero look different from the other digits?

Because it arrived separately. Unicode had circled one through nine from an earlier block and only later added a circled zero, ⓪ at U+24EA, in the Enclosed Alphanumerics range. A font that drew the two sets at different times can give the zero a slightly different ring size or weight than its neighbours.

Which part of this set breaks most often?

The lowercase letters. Some Android system fonts include the capitals from U+24B6 and stop there, so lowercase circled text turns into a row of empty rectangles on those devices. The digits are the most widely supported part of the block, and capitals are close behind them.

Can I use circled letters as list bullets?

That is one of the better uses for them. In a plain-text field with no list support, a circled letter or digit at the start of each line gives you numbered steps that survive copying, since the marker is part of the text. Keep to digits or capitals for the widest coverage.
